facts.statement: A partial skeleton of a large theropod was found in 1993 at the Phu Wiang 9 site in Khon Kaen by Somchai Traimwichanon.
facts.quote: In 1993, Somchai Traimwichanon found a partial skeleton of a large theropod at the Phu Wiang 9 site in Khon Kaen.

facts.statement: The species Siamotyrannus isanensis was named and described in 1996 by Eric Buffetaut, Varavudh Suteethorn, and Haiyan Tong.
facts.quote: In 1996, Eric Buffetaut, Varavudh Suteethorn and Haiyan Tong named and described the type species Siamotyrannus isanensis.

facts.statement: The holotype specimen PW9-1 was found in the Sao Khua Formation dating from the Berriasian to Barremian stages.
facts.quote: The holotype, PW9-1, was found in the Sao Khua Formation, dating from the Berriasian-Barremian.

facts.statement: Buffetaut estimated the length of Siamotyrannus at seven meters.
facts.quote: Buffetaut estimated its length at seven meters.

facts.statement: In 2010, Gregory S. Paul estimated the length at 6 meters and the weight at 500 kg.
facts.quote: In 2010, Gregory S. Paul estimated the length at 6 meters (20 ft), the weight at 500 kg.

facts.statement: In 2016, Molina-Pérez and Larramendi estimated the length at 10 meters and the weight at 1.75 tonnes.
facts.quote: In 2016 Molina-Pérez and Larramendi gave a higher estimation of 10 meters (33 ft) and 1.75 tonnes (1.93 short tons).

facts.statement: The second and third sacral vertebrae are strongly transversely flattened.
facts.quote: The second and third sacrals are strongly transversely flattened.

facts.statement: Although originally thought to be a tyrannosauroid or tyrannosaurid, its position in that group is uncertain due to lacking primary defining traits.
facts.quote: As evidenced by its name, it was originally thought to be a tyrannosauroid and even a tyrannosaurid, though due to lacking some of the primary tyrannosauroid synapomorphies that define the clade, its position there is not certain.

facts.statement: In 2012, Matthew Carrano et al. placed Siamotyrannus in the Metriacanthosaurinae.
facts.quote: In 2012 Matthew Carrano et al. found a position in the Metriacanthosaurinae.

facts.statement: In a 2024 review, Cau recovered Siamotyrannus as a tetanuran outside the Orionides and a close relative of Siamraptor.
facts.quote: In his 2024 review of theropod relationships, Cau recovered it as a tetanuran outside of the Orionides, as a close relative of Siamraptor.

facts.statement: Siamotyrannus isanensis is the only known species of the extinct genus Siamotyrannus, a metriacanthosaurid theropod dinosaur that lived in the Early Cretaceous between 129 and 113 million years ago in what is now Asia.
facts.quote: Siamotyrannus isanensis es la única especie conocida del género extinto Siamotyrannus ("tirano de Siam") de dinosaurio terópodo metriacantosáurido, que vivió en el Cretácico inferior, hace aproximadamente entre 129 a 113 millones de años, desde el Barremiense al Aptiense, en lo que hoy es Asia.

facts.statement: Fossils of Siamotyrannus consist of a pelvis and vertebrae found in Thailand within the Sao Khua Formation.
facts.quote: Los fósiles del Siamotyrannus consisten en una pelvis y vértebras que se encontraron en Tailandia, en la Formación Sao Khua.

facts.statement: In a 2024 review of theropod relationships, Cau found Siamotyrannus to be a tetanuran outside the Orionides clade and a close relative of Siamraptor.
facts.quote: En su revisión de 2024 de las relaciones de los terópodos, Cau encontró que sería un tetanuro situado por fuera del clado Orionides, siendo un pariente cercano de Siamraptor.

facts.statement: The parent group of Siamotyrannus is Metriacanthosaurinae.
Siamotyrannus belongs to the family Metriacanthosauridae.
Siamotyrannus lived during the Barremian stage, approximately 125.77 to 121.4 million years ago.
facts.quote: Time range: Barremian to Barremian (125.77 to 121.4 million years ago)
